title: GitHub Actions queued jobs: distinguish runner scheduling pressure from proven platform outage
scope: Bedrijfsgeheugen Powerhouse delivery and protected-gate execution

observations: Many workflows on the same exact candidate head completed successfully.
Required test subjobs preflight, automation, backend and portal completed successfully while website later acquired a runner and progressed.
Unified Brain Delivery candidate-identity completed successfully while plan remained queued on runs-on ubuntu-latest.
No self-hosted runner dependency was involved in the queued plan job.
The evidence therefore did not prove a GitHub-wide Actions outage; the observed state was compatible with transient GitHub-hosted runner scheduling or repository/account concurrency pressure.

root_cause_classification.confirmed: The delivery was waiting for GitHub-hosted runner allocation/scheduling for at least one protected job.
root_cause_classification.not_confirmed: A GitHub-wide external capacity incident or outage.
likely_contributors: A high number of workflows were triggered for the same candidate SHA.
Multiple jobs allocate ubuntu-latest runners independently.
Repository/account concurrency pressure can create transient queues even while other jobs continue to progress.

status_semantics.wrong_default: GEBLOKKEERD op externe GitHub Actions runner-capaciteit
hard_blocked_only_when: runner progress is absent beyond the configured bounded observation window
the exact required gate cannot obtain execution capacity
the queue condition is independently evidenced as a hard external boundary
safe recovery paths have been exhausted without bypassing protection

decision_order: Read exact-head workflow and job states.
Separate queued, in_progress, completed-success, failed and cancelled jobs.
Confirm runner class such as ubuntu-latest versus self-hosted labels.
Check whether sibling jobs on the same exact SHA are still acquiring runners and progressing.
Check repository/workflow concurrency configuration and duplicate-trigger pressure.
Check GitHub platform status as corroborating evidence, not as sole proof.
Do not label the incident a platform-wide outage or external-capacity hard block without independent evidence.
Do not create retrigger commits while the queue is demonstrably draining; that increases queue pressure and invalidates exact-head continuity.
Preserve branch protection and required checks; never bypass them to escape a queue.
recovery: Allow the existing exact-head run to continue while measurable progress exists.
Prefer deduplication and concurrency controls over repeated retriggers.
Only rerun a failed/cancelled job when evidence shows retry is appropriate; do not rerun merely because it is queued.
After all protected gates finish, continue normal exact-SHA merge, production readback and learning writeback.

engineering_improvement_targets: Use concurrency groups that cancel genuinely superseded work without cancelling the current exact-head authority.
Run only changed delivery lanes where contract coverage permits it.
Measure queue wait, execution duration, runner allocations and duplicate work as CI efficiency signals.
Escalate sustained queue delay separately from test failure so product defects and platform scheduling are never conflated.

evidence.candidate_commit_message: chore: retrigger exact-head gates after concurrency fix

applies_to: all existing and future Powerhouse agents
reuse_contract.required_behavior: Before declaring GEBLOKKEERD due to GitHub runner capacity, agents must classify the queue using this evidence hierarchy and preserve the current exact-head protected flow whenever it is still progressing.
